name: The Brand household — free Black Chicago, at the floor of its bracket
head: fb_brand_luther

composition_vector.what_is_carried: The SHAPE only — how many people, of which sex, in which band. No name, no age of any individual, no industry mark and no identity crosses from 1840 into this household.

free_black_household.stands_on: Caton's six certificates of freedom, August 1833, are the cohort's floor, and this is one of the six households the bracket's ceiling leaves room for. The SHAPE is the band vector of a Black-headed Chicago household of 1840 (printed page 215, line 29, FamilySearch image 33S7-9YYJ-9WF), dealt here as a structure and never as its people.
free_black_household.withdrawn_if: a reading that names Chicago's free Black residents of 1835, or a re-cut of the bracket that no longer leaves room for this household; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand

kin_owed.note: NO KIN TIE IS CLAIMED. The schedule of 1840 records no relationships at all, so everybody below the head is `household_member` and this stage writes no wife, no son and no daughter. The families of this cohort are owed to T-1170 and T-1171 exactly as every other household's are.

arrival.note: NOT DRAWN HERE. T-1169 owns the arrival fill, and the circle the trade households name holds here too: the arrival model is computed over the compiled scene and the scene carries these cards. One bound is on the record already — six men were at Chicago in August 1833, two years before the scene — and T-1169 is where it is spent.

lives_at.note: Not seated. T-1199 seats the reconstructed households on the lot grid by the placement policy, and nothing in this corpus says where Chicago's free Black residents lived in 1835. The division is `unplaced` and stays unplaced until it does.

works_at.note: Not seated. T-1189 staffs the businesses; the one firm this stage mints carries its keeper by id.

basis.note: Ordered by the bracket, not argued person by person: six free coloured men were certificated free at Chicago in August 1833 and the town's free Black population of 1840 scales back to 28 on the scene date. This household is one of the six the bracket carries.
